bull.b: Cloudflare is expanding rapidly while retaining and growing existing customers, indicating durable product adoption across its platform. Strong RPO growth and 122% net retention support continued recurring-revenue expansion as customers add products, increase usage, and enlarge commitments.

Substantial operating and free cash flow demonstrate that Cloudflare’s core subscription business converts growth into liquidity despite reported accounting losses. This cash generation can fund network investment, product development, and strategic execution while reducing reliance on external financing.

Lower operating expenses as a share of revenue show meaningful scalability in Cloudflare’s model. Management’s expectation of fourth-quarter GAAP profitability, substantially earlier than its prior outlook, suggests improving cost discipline could translate strong revenue growth into more durable earnings.

bear.b: The sharp increase in debt has materially reduced financial flexibility relative to the company’s equity base. Until profitability is consistently established, higher leverage can increase refinancing and interest obligations, constrain capital allocation, and make execution more sensitive to operating setbacks.

Cloudflare has improved substantially from earlier losses but has not yet demonstrated sustained GAAP profitability. Continued operating and net losses mean revenue growth is still required to support the cost structure, while any slower scaling could delay durable earnings and returns on equity.

Declining gross and free-cash-flow margins could limit how effectively Cloudflare converts strong demand into earnings and liquidity. Although gross margin remains within management’s long-term range, continued compression would weaken operating leverage and reduce cash available for investment or debt management.
